Suspended—kʼakatzʼininoq.
Calm—kʼakachamamoq.
At rest—kʼakatzʼinonik.
Silent—kʼasilanik.
No murmur—kʼakalolinik.

Not yet one animal—Jun Chikop.
No bird—Tzʼikin.

Just Sky alone. Face of Earth cannot be seen.

section: The Still Sea, The Empty Sky, pp. 4-5
body:
Still silent Sea. Settled, calm, quiet.
Wombed over by vast vacant void of empty vault of Sky.
Separate—the two who are pooled together.
Perfect reflection: One over Other.
Two seen as just One—xa Jun.
Mirrored void: vacant Sky reflected in silent Sea.
Serene silent Sky floats on placid pool of Sea.
Silent stillness echoes in emptiness of reflected quiet.
One reveals Other in mirror Sky, on mirror Sea.
Nothing yet gathered. Nothing yet sounding.
Nothing to rise. Nothing to move.
Everything at rest. Everything held.
Just nothing there to stand. Just nothing to climb up, out, about.
Just nothing there to shoot up, sprout out.
Xa ma kʼo wi naki laʼ kʼolik yakalik.
Just pooled Water. Just flat Sea.
Calm, collected. Placid, pooled.
All that might exist—not yet.
All that might be—not yet.

Nocturnal darkness.
Dark of night.
Where all is silent dark of night.

In darkness. In night.
All alone yet together. Together as one.
Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol—Former, Shaper.
Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz—Sovereign Plumed Serpent.
Alom, Kʼajolom—Bearer, Begetter.

Precious quetzal feathers. Lovely blue cotinga plumage.

Former-Shaper. Bearer-Begetter.
Just out of view:
Enveloped in jade feathers.
Bundled in turquoise plumage.
Awash in sparkling iridescent blue-green waters.
Emerald green Sea glistening, glimmering, glittering.
Blue-black darkness of Sky.
Cloaked in mantle of calm quiet.
Dark womb of night.
Water-Sky.
Starlight sparkles in starlit night.
Shines, shivers—silver slivers of scintillating light.
Shimmers, shines bright at midnight.
Glittering waters glisten, glimmer, glint, gleam.
Flash, flicker, shake, shiver, quake, quiver.
All about Sacred Bundle of his Majesty:
Lord Quetzalcoatl—Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz—Sovereign Plumed Serpent.
Enveloped, enclosed, encased in emerald cloak.
Flutters, floats like cypress bows rippling in breeze.
Covers Precious Twin Quetzalcoatl in plumed mantle of jade serpents.
Wrapped in soft embrace of feathery fluff of fine fluorescent feathers.
Twinned, coupled. Paired, doubled.
Complementary, complete.
Divine twins bundled, bound together.
Precious plumage:
Resplendent Quetzal—Qʼuqʼ—emerald green.
Lovely Blue Cotinga—Raxon—turquoise blue.
Two become one. Ancient ancestral embrace.
Envelops, embodies:
Everlasting life of jade green seed.
Lifeʼs eternal return.
Deathʼs undying renewal.

Sacred Bundle of Quetzal Feathers.
Preciously twinned with Lovely Blue Cotinga Plumage.
Perfect complements of one another.
This sacred bundle bears within its embrace:
Essence of creation.
Resplendent jade green jewel of maize kernel.
Luminous blue mask of watery wet light.
Emerald reed. Jade seed. Turquoise bead.
Soon to be brought forth:
From shadowy darkness into resplendent light.
Soil, Sky, Sea. Earth, Air, Water.
Dusty-dirt of earth. Rich resinous green Cypress bows.
Earth-Sky. Water-Sky. Sea-Earth. Sky-Earth.
Paired with one another:
Iridescent green, red, white Feathers of Resplendent Quetzal.
Golden amber, earthen brown, obsidian black of Rattlesnakeʼs Serpent Scales.
Two beings:
Earth and Sea. Sky and Earth. Sky and Sea.
Form, shape this Precious Twin:
Blue and green. Turquoise and jade.
Gold and obsidian. Silver and coral red.
Emerald and gold.
Feathered Serpent. Plumed Serpent. Quetzalcoatl. Qʼuqʼ-Kumatz.
Eternal return never comes too early.
Rising as Morning Star never comes too late.

His Word—Tzij—came together here.
Where Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz—Sovereign Plumed Serpent—was.
In darkness—chi qʼequmal.
In night—chi aqʼabʼal.
Heart of Sky—Ukʼuʼx Kaj—spoke with Sovereign Plumed Serpent—Tepew
Qʼuqʼkumatz.
They brought their Word together in Council.
They gathered together their thoughts.
They pondered. They wondered.
Considerate—their contemplation of thoughts.
Concerned—when they contemplated imagination.
When they consulted thinking of thoughts.
There where they came together as One in deliberation.
There in dark. There in night.

These are those known as:
Heart of Sky—Ukʼux Kaj.
Heart of Lake-Sea—Ukʼuʼx Cho-Palo.

People who would populate Face of Earth.
They knew as they thought.
Just as they saw as they imagined.
Way their creation would be brought forth.
Through clarity of thinking.
Through ingenuity of imagination.
Bring human life—kʼaslem—to fruition.
Bring creation of human beings—winaqirem—to completion.
They, the two Kabʼawil:
Ukʼuʼx Kaj.
Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz.

There before light of dawn—ta xkikʼuxlaj kibʼ xeʼ wi saq.

Revealed through genius of imagination.
Image that told them, showed them:
How they would bring about birth of life.
Lead to creation of humanity: utzʼuquxik kʼaslem, winaqirem!
Thought that was image that was vision of imagination.
Showed them, told them:
How to bring about sprouting out of life.
Lead to sprouting forth of all being.
Come to fruition through sprouting forth of humanity.

Generation of human condition—winaqirem.

Xa Nawal—just their magical powers of transformation.
Xa Pus—just their giving of sacrifice.
Made it so.
Their way of thinking upon sprouting forth—xwinaqirik—of Earth.
Made it so.
Just their transformative genius alone.
Creative imagination alone.
Conceived of nawal creation.
Brought forth to completion, to fruition.
Forming. Shaping.
Molding. Modeling.
Mountain-Plain: Juyubʼ-Taqʼaj.

Face of Earth covered with cypress groves.
Blanketed with pine groves—ukisisil, upachajil.
Cypress groves, pine groves sprouted forth across mountainside.
Mantle of cypress cloaked mountain.
Mantle of pine blanketed Mountain-Plain: Juyub, Taqʼaj.
Great Mountain enveloped in Great Many Trees.
Blanketed with mantle of Cypress Groves—Kisisil—of Maize Lord Quetzalcoatl.
Cloaked with mantle of Torch Pine Groves—Pachajil—of Tojil—Sun Deity—Lord
Torch—Lord Lightning-Bolt.
Cypress Trees, Torch-Pine Trees formed, shaped green groves.
Covered Face of Earth with thick mantle of verdure.
Cloaked mountainside with resplendent emerald and jade green perfection.
Two Kabʼawil made present in form of their Nawal Transforms.
Sky-Earth prepared for forming, shaping of Providers, Sustainers.

Indeed Qʼuqʼkumatz made content.
Contentment called upon him to speak with Heart of Sky—Ukʼuʼx Kaj:
"Is it not good that you have come, you Ukʼuʼx Kaj; you Jun Raqan; and you Chʼipi
Kaqulja; and you Raxa Kaqulja?"
"Our Forming, our Shaping has turned out well," they replied.
And so it did.
Their Forming, their Shaping did turn out well.
First, then—Earth made to arise as Mountain-Plain.
Then next—natural course of water found its way.
Down through mountainside.
Form rivers, streams winding down Great Mountain when it appeared.
Earth created—uwinaqirik.
Made to sprout up and out—xwinaqirik—of Water.
By Heart of Sky, Heart of Earth: Ukʼuʼx Kaj, Ukʼuʼx Ulew.

Sky made to exist. Earth too made to exist.
To then be placed in Water.

Sky sidled up to one side.
Earth sidled up to other side.
To then be placed amongst Waters.
Sky brought forth into being.
Earth too brought forth.
To then be placed amidst Water.
Sky made. Earth too made.
To then be set within Water.
These then were their thoughts.
This then their thinking.
When they considered their work, their work of creation.
When they wondered, pondered all they had done.
When they thought about all they had brought to completion.
When they contemplated all they had done to bring work to conclusion.
This then how they finished their work:
Bringing forth Sky-Earth.

body:
By Former, Shaper; Molder, Modeler
They thought upon their bringing forth:
Wild Animals of Mountain Wilderness—Uchikopil Juyubʼ.
They imagined, envisioned:
Populating mountainside with Animals.
They thought upon their bringing forth:
Forest Guardians—Chajal re Kʼichelaj.
They considered, contemplated:
Populating Forest with Keepers, Care-takers of Mountain Wilderness—Uwinaqil
Juyubʼ.
They imagined forest beings.
They thought upon animals of mountains, guardians of forest.
First attempt to populate mountainside with animals.
First attempt to populate wilderness with guardians of forest.
Caretakers of wilderness.
Many animals would come to people wild mountain-plain.
Animals would come to populate mountain wilderness:
uchikopil juyubʼ, chajal re kiʼchelaj ronojel uwinaqil juyubʼ.
Before long:
Imaginative thinking inspired nawal genius.
Brought forth images of animal protectors.
Animal guardians would come to reside among Trees and Vines.
These imagined would come to inhabit many trees of forest.
There upon Mountain-Plain known as Juyubʼ-Taqʼaj.

body:
Bearer-Begetter—Alom, Kʼajolom—spoke:
"Should there just be din of silence?
Should there only be deafening quiet under Trees and Vines?
If so, then best they have Guardians—Chajal—to watch over them!"
Said Mother-Fathers: Alom, Kʼajolom.
"Should there be such din of silence?
Nothing more than tranquil rustling of savage serene quiet?
That incessant sort of horrendous hush in bush amongst brush?
Just relentless roar of stillness beneath branches?
Flowering vines and fruiting trees with all their spiny thorns and many stinging
leaves?
Was this only speech ever to be spoken here on Earth?
Earth that had yet to be awoken?"

With hoofed feet and feathered wings.
Their speech made it so.
Immediately these forest beings brought forth.
Instantly, just like that—jusukʼ—made to appear:
Deer—Kej.
Bird—Tzʼikin.
Four-Footed Ones.
Feathery Winged-Ones.
Instantly came into being.
There in Mountains. There in Canyons.
Down in Ravine among Trees and upon Vines.

section: They Were Given Their Abode, pp. 19-20
body:
Deer, Birds—given their homes:
"You, Deer, go down there by river. Go sleep in ravines, in canyons. There you
shall live."
"Here is where you shall be:
In grasslands, among wild fruit trees.
Up in branches. Out on vines. In forest.
This is where you will grow and multiply.
On all four you will move about. On all four you will make your way.
This is how it will be."
This is what was said to them.
This is what they were told.
Then next they chose living places.
Mountain abode. Place in valley.
Homes of Small Birds. Big Birds:
"You, you Birds, get on up in trees.
There up above in branches.
Up, up, on top of vines.
Make your nests. Build your homes.
There, there is where you will multiply to become many.
There, there is where you will grow and increase.
There on limbs, there on branches of trees.
Out on vines is where you will be."
This is what they were told when they were spoken to:
Deer, Birds.
Four-Footed Ones and those of Feathered-Wings.

body:
Being given sleeping places, burrows, dens.
Gathering what was there to make dwellings.
Fashion houses. Build homes.
There in forest they went to live.
There in wilderness is where they fashioned nests, dens, lairs.
Some slept together. Others slept alone.
Some lived with one another. Others lived on their own.
This was way Animals of Wilderness, Animals of Earth were each given home.
By Alom, Kʼajolom—Bearer, Begetter—as they are known.

And so it was that they:

Bringing forth:
Deer, Birds.
Four-Footed Ones, those of Feathery Wings.

body:
When work was complete, when work was finished:
Former, Shaper; Bearer, Begetter—Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom—called upon
Deer and Birds.
To do what they were Formed to do.
What they were Shaped to do.
Invoke their Former. Invoke their Shaper.
They who Formed were Formers.
Just as They who were Shaped were Those who were Shapers.
Former—Tzʼaqol, Shaper—Bʼitol—those who Formed, those who Shaped.
Those who were Formed Ones, those who were Shaped Ones: AjTzʼaq, AjBʼit.
Now Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom wanted to be remembered.
Being invoked by those they had Formed.
Wanted to be remembered by those they had Shaped.
Those who were Former, Shaper; Mother, Father; Bearer, Begetter:
Wished only to hear, in order to feel, their names being named.
By Animals who they created:
Deer—Kej.
Bird—Tzʼikin.
Those called up to name the names.
Of their Former, their Shaper; Bearer, Begetter:
Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom.
And so they ordered Animal People to do just this.

source: Popol Wuj: Layered Mythic Language (telegraphic rendering of the Stanzione translation)
section: They Spoke to Deer, to Birds, pp. 22-24
body:
They were spoken to by Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom:
"Speak out! Call out!
Donʼt just squawk. Donʼt just warble.
Invoke us: each one of you one by one.
According to your class, your kind.
According to your group, your order.
Go ahead now just Name our Names!"
This is what was said to them:
ri Kej—the Deer
Tzʼikin—Birds
Koj—Puma
Bʼalam—Jaguar
Kumatz—Serpent
"Name then our names.
Show us reverence, show us respect.
Invoke us, name us:
We, your Mother; We, your Father—Oj Ichuch; Oj Iqajaw!"
"Go ahead; get right to it.
You can do it; nowʼs the time for you to prove it.
Go ahead, just do it!"
"Go ahead, just do what youʼve been asked to do.
Show us regard, show us respect.
Name our names just like this:"
Jun Raqan, Chʼipi Kaqulja, Raxa Kaqulja
Ukʼuʼx Kaj, Ukʼuʼx Ulew
Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol
Alom, Kʼajolom
"Speak forth, speak out! Kixchaʼwoq!"
"Invoke us; remember us; revere us.
Show us regard; show us respect.
Worship us in our way.
This is all we ask you to say.
Just give us thanks; just show us praise: Kojiqʼijila!"
"Go ahead, just do it: Name our Names!"
They were ordered, when they were spoken to: Xeʼuchaʼxik.

body:
They couldnʼt do it.
They could not speak like their Former, Shaper: Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol asked of them.
They just mimicked sound and speech of others.
When they began to speak:
They just squawked and screeched.
Instead of making proper speech they just shrieked.
They just whined, whimpered.
They just chittered, chattered.
They just howled and yowled when they wanted growl.
They just kept up shrill squeaking and squawking.
Acting as if they were really talking.
They could only moan and groan all alone.
Instead of talking amongst one another as desired by their Mother-Father: Alom,
Kʼajolom.
Now it was known, being clearly shown:
Animals could not and would not speak like their Mother-Father.
Animals could not talk amongst one another as asked to do:
Speak common language between one another that sound true.
Speak as group, as class, as order, as single kind.
Communicate together with one another.
To then Name the Names of those who formed and shaped them.
Their Former, their Shaper.
No longer clear as to nature of language they spoke.
Each one of them cried out as they called out in different ways.
Each one with their own form of speech.
As difficult to speak as it was to repeat.
Expression, character, nature of their language never came out clearly.
Each one of them cried out in different ways.
Each according to their kind.
All according to their group.
Each speaking speech that was theirs and theirs alone.

source: Popol Wuj: Layered Mythic Language (telegraphic rendering of the Stanzione translation)
section: Their Work Had Not Turned Out Good (part 1), pp. 25-27
body:
When Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol heard them:
They knew their work had not turned out good.
Animals, as hard as they tried:
Could not speak with one another as their creators wished they would.
Most definitely thought there should.
Former, Shaper talked it over together.
As they spoke with one another.
To then say what they said:
"Naming of our Names by formed beings we formed, by shaped beings we
shaped did not turn out well.
This is just not right just as it is just no good."
Said Alom, Kʼajolom speaking together as companions of one another: chi kibʼil
kibʼ.
So, then, they said:
"You must be transformed. You must be transfigured.
You did not turn out way we imagined you to be.
As those who speak together in one form of speech.
You cannot speak one language together.
You cannot speak with one another.
Like we speak as your Father, your Mother.
So why try anymore, why even bother."
"Now you have forced us to bring you down.
We must change our word.
We must change what we said about way you are to live in forest.
We must change your life ways.
We must change your sustenance, your sleeping places, your homes, yours lairs.
We must change very living spaces we gave to you as your dwelling place.
Your earthly abode. Your residence here in world on Face of Earth."
They were told.
"All that is yours will come from canyons and ravines and from forest.
Because you could not revere us through remembrance Our Days."
They said.
"Nor could you worship us by showing us praise.
Through veneration and reverence that comes with sacred act of Naming our
Names.
As you were created to do."
They added.
"You could not invoke us, nor summons us.
By calling upon us as we formed and shaped you to do."
"There are those who will come to do what we ask of them.
Those who will show us reverence through orderly practice of our orderly
ancestral ways.
Orderly naming of our names in perfectly ordered sacred ways.
By giving us praise in ancestral ways that keep count of our numbered and named
days."
Said Bearer, spoke Begetter: Alom, Kʼajolom.
"For there will be those who will provide for us with sacrificial offerings.
Offerings sacrificed to us that will provide and sustain us with sacred sustenance."

section: Their Work Had Not Turned Out Good (part 2), pp. 25-27
body:
"So just bear your fate.
This shall be your destiny for rest of your days:
Let your flesh be eaten!"
"Ta chuxoq! May it come to pass! Let it be so!
This, then, is your beneficial burden, your ancestral debt, your divine duty, your
sacred service.
To all those who will live from your death to thrive from your flesh."
As it was said so they were told.

section: When They Met Their Defeat, pp. 27-28
body:
Then Small Animals, Big Animals were instructed.
As to what was their fate when they were given counsel.
As to what their destiny was here on Face of Earth.
Then they met their defeat.
When their flesh became meat to feed hunger and appetite.
Of those who would come to eat them as sweet sort of treat.
Ancestral destiny. Divine burden of Animal People.
Here on Face of Earth where fate of flesh:
Flesh of Small Animals and flesh of Big Animals.
To be hunted and killed to be eaten as meat.
Meat to be eaten as sacred sustenance of other animals.
Here on Face of Earth: Chuwach Ulew.

source: Popol Wuj: Layered Mythic Language (telegraphic rendering of the Stanzione translation)
body:
SO IT WAS THEN THAT ANOTHER EFFORT WAS MADE
To bring forth Formed People, Shaped People—Winaq Tzʼaq, Winaq Bʼit.
By Former, Shaper; Bearer, Begetter—Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom.
"Let us just try again. Let us make another attempt.
For is not Sowing, Dawning soon upon us?"
"Xa kʼu tija chik mixyopij rawexik, usaqirik?"
"Let us make Formed Being that provides for us.
Let us make Shaped Being that sustains us.
One who nourishes us. One who nurtures us.
As Our Provider, as Our Sustainer.
Those spoken of as Feeder, those named as Maintainer—Tzuqul, Kʼool—as they
shall be known."
"If not, then who?
Who will Name our Names through our invocation?
Who then will remember us through remembrance of our ways here upon Face of
Earth?"
"Did we not already try with our First Forming, with our First Shaping?
Did we not already complete our Molding and Modeling?
Of those who would worship us by being and becoming?
Those who would come forth to count and keep our Divine Days?
Those who would venerate us in honorable, benevolent ways?
Those who would regard and respect us by showing us thanks and praise?
As our Day-Keepers?
Those who would become our Keeper and Counter of Days—qaqʼijiloxik?"
"Did we not already finish work of Crafting and Creating?
Those who would become our Prayer-makers and Worshippers?
To bring about Our Glorification before our Throne and its Altar Place?
Where we were to receive our adoration, our adulation, our worship and our
admiration—qaqʼalajxik?"
"Did we not already bring forth those who would glorify and worship us?
With their adoration and glorification of us?
As our Prayer-Makers and Worshippers who would invoke us and remember us?
Through showing us praise and glory—qaqʼalajxik—in ancestral ways?
Through their worship and praise of us?
By Keeping Sacred Count of Our Sacred Days in sacred, sacrificial ways?"
"Did we not already attempt to make Obedient One—AjNim?
Who was Humble One—AjXobʼ?
Who was Respectful One—AjXobʼ?
Who was Devout One—AjNim?
Who would be those known as Our Provider; Our Sustainer?
Those named: Tzuqul; Kʼool."
They cried as they wept.
"So then, shall we not try again?"

section: The Man of Mud — Xoq'ol (part 1), pp. 30-32
body:
They formed his body from Ulew—Earth.
His flesh was made of mud—xoqʼol.
For it was mud that was clay—xoqʼol.
That they molded and modeled flesh—utyoʼjil.
Of body of this being formed from Earth—Ulew.
This creature created from clay—xoqʼol.
This man made of mud—xoqʼol.
So then it didnʼt look so good: Ma kʼu utz xkilo
So then they didnʼt like way it looked: Ma kʼu utz xkilo
So then they didnʼt look upon it with contentment: Ma kʼu utz xkilo
Just lop-sided, deformed, incoherent, inconsistent: xa chi yojomanik
Just soft, spongy, squishy, squashy, without character: xa tzubʼulik
Just soggy, sopping wet, saturated, it could not move: xa nebʼelik
Just so weak, without strength, limp, it just crumbled: xa lubʼanik
Just one to come undone, it fell apart, it fell to pieces, it fell over: xa wulanik
And it just dissolved in water when it got wet: xa pu chiʼumarik
And so it just melted away; it became soft; it was weak: xa pu chiʼumarik
His head was not round so it drooped to one-side: Mawi chi kʼolol ujolom
His head sagged so that he couldnʼt hold it up: Mawi chi kʼolol ujolom
Not being round his skull would never roll: Mawi chi kʼolol ujolom
His head could not swivel around: Mawi chi kʼolol ujolom
He could not turn his head around: Mawi chi kʼolol ujolom
He could not spin his head about: Mawi chi kʼolol ujolom
Just in one direction could he face: Xa jun bʼenaq wi uwach
He could just look in one direction: Xa jun bʼenaq wi uwach
Just lop-sided was his twisted face: Xa jun bʼenaq wi uwach
He just faced in one direction: Xa jun bʼenaq wi uwach
His face was just immovable; fixed; motionless: Xa jun bʼenaq wi uwach
His face was stationary; still; stiff; unmoving: Xa jun bʼenaq wi uwach
He could just walk in one direction since he could only see in one direction!
Just blanketed was his vision: Xa kuʼl uwach
Just covered-up was his sight: Xa kuʼl uwach
Just veiled was his vision: Xa kuʼl uwach
He could not see behind him: Mawi chi mukun chirij
He couldnʼt see what was coming: Mawi chi mukun chirij
He couldnʼt see what was coming up from behind: Mawi chi mukun chirij
He couldnʼt look back: Mawi chi mukun chirij
Chi chʼaw nabʼe maja bʼi unaʼoj; xa jusukʼ chiʼumar pa jaʼ.

source: Popol Wuj: Layered Mythic Language (telegraphic rendering of the Stanzione translation)
section: The Man of Mud — Xoq'ol (part 2), pp. 30-32
body:
He spoke at first but he had no genius; just right away he dissolved in water.
He spoke at first but without intelligence; he just crumbled before falling apart
when placed in water.
He could speak in beginning but unable to make himself understood for he had no
insight; he just instantly softened up before melting away in water.
At first he communicated but without understanding; he just immediately came
undone; to quickly dissolve in water.
He spoke at first but without insight; he just immediately disintegrated in water!
Chi chʼaw nabʼe maja bʼi unaʼoj; xa jusukʼ chiʼumar pa jaʼ.
"Heʼs not hard; he will not endure!" said Former; said Shaper.
"Mawi Ko!" xechaʼ chi ku ri AjTzʼaq; AjBʼit.
"He will never last; he just isnʼt strong enough," said Former, said Shaper.
"It is just sign of what not to do; itʼs warning of further failures that lie up ahead; it
is just indication of whatʼs to come! So be it!"
"It is just mistake; he canʼt even walk; it is best he never be allowed to multiply to
become great many more mistakes."
"This man made of mud; this crafted clay creature; this fallen, failed, flawed
formation formed from flesh of earth is just no good."
"It is just been test; itʼs just been another attempt of our forming and shaping that
has come to bad end; itʼs just another failure, another flawed work of crafting
creation; itʼs real flop."
"It is just mistake; itʼs just omen is what it is; just sign; premonition: xa labʼeq! So
be it! We will just have to think it over again," they said.

This is when they threw him down.
When they laid him low.
His Molders. His Modelers.
They just took their clay creation up in their hands.
Brought him crashing down to ground.
They smashed their failed formation to pieces on Earth below!
It was over. They could begin again.
And they did by asking:
"What should we do now? ¿Jupa cha ki chiqabʼano?"

A Third Try; A Third Attempt; A Third Endeavor
To Carve Obedient Ones—AjNim; to Create Respectful Ones—*AjXobʼ*
To Form Providers—Tzuqul; to Shape Sustainers—*Kʼool*
They began again.
When they wondered. When they pondered.
When they thought. When they contemplated.
Upon what was to be done next.
To bring their work of forming to completion.
To bring their work of shaping to conclusion.
"What shall we do to finish our work to form, our work to shape?
Those who will name our names?
Those who will keep our days?
Those who will remember us in sacred ways?"
This is what they said when they thought on it again.
When they imagined it just so.
Just so they could bring forth formed beings who were shaped beings.
Who would worship them by giving them praise by keeping their days.
This was what they said when they thought on it again.
When they imagined it so they would see how to carve and create beings.
Who would invoke then.
So that they would know how to form and shape those who would remember
them.
Through ancestral ways of remembrance.

section: They Went to the Diviners, pp. 34-35
body:
They went to Diviners of Destiny.
Those who formed and shaped golden seeds of maize and coral red beans of
divination.
Those known and named:
Xpiyakok, Xmuqane; Junajpu Wuch, Junajpu Utiw.
Grandfather Possum, Lord of Dawn.
Grandfather Coyote, Lord of Night.
"Let us just speak with those who are Xpiyakok, Xmuqane; Junajpu Wuch,
Junajpu Utiw.
Let them make another attempt to see again what must be done.
To divine destiny of our Forming and Shaping Formed Ones, Shaped Ones.
To divine fortune and fate of our Carving and Creating Carved Ones, Created
Ones."
"Letʼs just do what we must do:
To consult count of Days.
To consult Ancient Ways.
To consult Forming of Tzʼite Beans.
To consult Shaping of Maize Seeds."
"Let us take up that which is casting of Sacred Seeds of Sortilege.
Let us take up that which is casting of Divine Beans of Divination."
"Which is to say:
We must cast consultation of beans.
Divination of seeds to see what shape forming takes.
To see what form shaping makes.
So that we can know form our casting makes.
To know shape our divination takes."

body:
Those who are known as:
Xpiyakok, Xmuqane; Junajpu Wuch, Junajpu Utiw
Cast and count:
Golden seeds of Maize Tree—Ixim Cheʼ.
Red beans of Coral Tree—Tzʼite Tree.
They said:
"With kernels and beans let us cast our destiny.
Let us count-out our futureʼs fate.
So that we may see form.
So that we may see shape of face that our divination takes.
With coral red beans of Tzʼiteʼ Tree.
With golden yellow kernels of Maize Tree—Ixim Cheʼ."
This is what was said by those who are spoken of as:
AjTzʼaq, AjBʼit—Divine Ancestors of Forming, Divine Ancestors of Shaping.
Known as Former, known as Shaper—Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol.
When they spoke to Ancestral Couple; Ancestral Pair; Ancient Ones.
Nawal Winaq; Nawinaq—Ancestral Magicians.
As they are known and named:
Xpiyakok, Xmuqane.
"Let us just speak with Xpiyakok, Ixmuqane.
Let us just consult with Jun AjPu Wuch, Jun AjPu Utiw.
Ancient Ones. Ancestral Couple. Primordial Pair.
Those who are Seers. Those who are Knowers.
They who are Diviners.
Those who will know just what we must do.
To bring our Forming and Shaping to fruition."
"Let us, let them make another attempt.
To see what there is to be seen through their sacred forming.
To know what there is to be known through their sacred shaping."
"Let us, let them make another attempt.
To bring forth their Divine Count of Days.
Formation of its Ancestral Ways.
To see in order to know what form their Sacred Count of Days takes."
"Let us, let them form and shape their Divination.
To see what we seek to see.
To know what we need to know.
So that we come to see and know what we need to do.
To form and shape Our Forming; Our Shaping.
To Carve and Craft Our Creation of Formed Ones; of Shaped One; of Carved
Ones; of Crafted Ones.
Let it be done."
"Let us; let them make another effort.
To bring forth their insight and imagination through their divination.
Through their counting and their shaping of divine count and sacred shape of their
divination."
"Let us; let them mold and model their Ancestral Divination.
To reveal what is to be known.
Through their powers of revelation that comes through those who are Diviners—
AjQʼij—Day-Keepers.
Knowers—AjNaʼoj—Wise Ones.

source: Popol Wuj: Layered Mythic Language (telegraphic rendering of the Stanzione translation)
section: The Ancestral Couple — Xpiyakok, Ixmuqane (part 1), pp. 37-41
body:
Xpiyakok, Ixmuqane: Ancestral Couple, Primordial Pair.
Junajpu Wuch, Junajpu Utiw.
Nawal Winaq—Magically Transforming Ancestors.
Who take form and shape of their Animal Companions.
Their Animal Souls. Their Animal Guides.
Spirit Guides of Dead, of Dawn, of Dark, of Night and its Darkness.
These are those from Ancient Age of Animal People.
Where anima-soul-psyche—ukʼuʼx—is very heart and soul.
And of word anima-animal.
Xpiyakok, Ixmuqane work together as diviners.
To find out what to form and shape.
Next attempt of peopling and populating Face of Earth.
They work as pair.
One is pillar—raqan.
Other is former and shaper of destiny.
Who scatters and shapes, counts and forms:
Seeds and beans of ancient practice of divination.
Maya have practiced since time immemorial.
Two Ancestral Diviners introduced and named:
Grandmothers of Dawn, Grandmothers of Light.
It is they who divine through their ancient ancestral animal soul, animal spirit.
Xpiyakok is known as Junajpu Wuch.
Ancient Ancestral Animal Soul of Dawn.
Embodied by Junajpu Wuch.
Translated as Old Man Possum—Junajpu Wuch.
Powerful Lord of Dawn, Lord of Underworld.
For Xpiyakok already dead by time stories of his sons and grandsons begin.
Wuch or Possum smells of Land of Dead and Lords of Dead.
Ancestors are Dead.
So it is Dead Ancestors who provide and sustain their Descendants.
With Divinatory Knowledge through day-dreaming insights and night-dreaming
journeys.
Of soul, anima, animal soul—nawal or nagual or nahual—animal spirit.
Of each and every Diviner and Day-Keeper, Prayer-Maker and Petitioner.
Who works on behalf of their people and pueblo.
To find path that must be taken.
To do what needs to be done.
To bring about creation or destruction.
These Animal Transforms, Animal Companions known as:
Junajpu Wuch, Junajpu Utiw.
Spoken of here as Junajpu Wuch:
Ancient Ancestral One Grandfather Possum.
Noble Lord and Grandfather of Dawn: Junajpu Wuch.
Whereas Ixmuqane is known to Kʼicheʼ Maya Day-Keepers and Prayer-Makers as:
Ix-Muq-Qʼanil.
Or She of Buried Mazorca.
She of Buried Maize Seed.
Whose womb is womb of earth where maize seed is sown.
To sprout forth as milpa in which many sons come into existence.

section: The Ancestral Couple — Xpiyakok, Ixmuqane (part 2), pp. 37-41
body:
As Four Hundred Boys of South.
Where South is seen as Place Thick with Abundance.
Because of Heat and Rain found their when Sun moves to South from May to
November.
Rainy season and growing season of maize.
Ixmuqane, like many other Maize Mothers of Ancient Americas:
Is sacrificed and her body so that it may be buried.
Transformed into maize and squash, cacao and herb.
As well as many other fruits and vegetables.
Important point to understand:
Ancient Ancestors bodies become sacred sustenance of their descendants.
Ixmuqane also known as Jun AjPu Utiw.
Or Ancient One Grandmother Coyote.
Ixmuqane as Jun AjPu Utiw come from:
Ancient Ancestral Place of Reeds spoken of as Jun AjPu.
Ancient Ancestral Place Thick with Abundance.
Ancient Ancestral Place Thick with Reeds.
Ixmuqane in this section we are entering here:
Known as Ancient Grandmother Diviner, Grandmother Coyote of Dusk.
Jun Ajpu Utiw known as:
Ancient Ancestral Coyote Grandmother, Ruler and Authority of Night.
She feeds off Death.
She transforms as she wishes.
For she is Trickster Deity Extraordinaire with Magical Powers of Transformation.
That when understood are at very center of Popol Wujʼs sacred narrative.
Xpiyakok, Ixmuqane as Primordial Couple of Ancient Ancestral Trickster Diviners:
Those who know everything there is to know.
Because they come from Ancient Age, Ancient Sun of Animal People.
This is what makes them such powerful diviners.
As Primordial Couple or Ancient Ones:
They are rulers of knowledge of divination.
Given to those who see in dark and live in night.
While resting in Light of Day.
When Sunʼs power overtakes powers of diviners who cannot see when there is so
much light.
Ancient Word says:
"Let us speak with them that they might speak through their divination.

section: They Looked with Ancestral Vision, pp. 41-42
body:
There were they looked with their ancestral vision.
To know and reveal what was asked of them.
By those who sought to see what they saw with their powers of divination.
These were those who were Mid-Most Seers—Nikʼ Wachinel.
Whose vision saw what there was to see.
In order to know what there was to be known.
What they saw and knew was then revealed.
As knowledge they sought with their seeds and stones.
With their beans and bones that formed and shaped their divination.
Of all that could be seen to be known.
This is what they revealed to Jun Raqan and Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz.
When they were spoken to by:
AjQʼij; AjBʼit; e NikʼWachinel.
These are those who are known as:
AjQʼij—Day-Keepers.
These are those who are counters and keepers of Sacred Days.
As well as those who reveal their revelation of destiny in Sacred Ways.
These are those who are seers and diviners of days.
That see and divine through their ancient ancestral powers of divination.
These are those known as:
AjBʼit—Former of Divination; Shaper of Divination.
Those who form small mounds of seeds for formation of divination.
Those who shape small mounds of beans for creation of divination.
These are those who are known as:
e NikʼWachinel.
Those who are Mid-Most Seers of divinatory imagination.
That is seen to be known as inner-most vision of seeing and knowing.
In Ancestral Art and Science of Divination.
These are those known as e NikʼWachinel.
Who were Mid-Most Seers that could see to very Heart of Revelation of Divination.
It was they who saw into very Center of Revelation of Divination.

body:
Maya Prayer-Making; Kʼicheʼ Day-keeping
"Invoke us so that we might be invoked by our Descendants.

By those who are Worshipful Ones.
By those who are Loyal Ones, those who Faithful Ones.
By those who are Devout; Devoted Ones.
By those who are Dedicated, Dutiful Ones.
So that we might be remembered.
So that we might be honored.
By those who are Our Providers; Our Sustainers."
Xpiyakok; Ixmuqane:
These are those who are Grandmother, Grandfather—Qatiʼt, Qamam.
Who are also known as Iyom, Mamom—Midwife, Matchmaker.
Who are Ancestral Couple; Ancestral Pair.
Who bring their Granddaughters; Grandsons into world.
As their Descendants known as Iweey—their Descendants; their Teeth!
Iyom comes from Eeyʼom:
Grandmother; Mid-wife who brings forth her Descendants; her Teeth.
Teeth that are Maize Seed that bring forth Descendants of Maize!
Xpiyakok; Ixmuqane are Grandmother, Grandfather of their Grandchildren.
Who are their descendants who are replacements of their Grandmother,
Grandfather—Qatiʼt, Qamam.
Of Maize People—Ixim Winaq.
Those who are People and Pueblo of Maize—Ixim Winaq.
Ixim Winaq are those who live together in their Pueblo of Maize People.
That is like Milpa of Maize; Corn Field.
Whose ancestral story is told here.
In mythopoetic mythic metaphorical speech.
Known as Ancient Ancestral Account—Ojer Tzij.
Of those who are known as Ixim Winaq.
Whose Ancient Word—Ojer Tzij—we bring forth here.
As remembrance of their Ancient Ancestral Grandmother, Grandfather—Qatiʼt,
Qamam.
Who are none other than Xpiyakok; Ixmuqane.
Who are none other than those known as Mid-Wife, Matchmaker; Matriarch;
Patriarch—Iyom, Mamom.
Of Ixim Winaq.
This is their story and it is they who are Diviners and Day-keepers.
Who bring about this entire myth.
So it is best you meet them now!
Same hands that will now perform forming and shaping of divination.
That is about to happen here.
So now you are well prepared for her hands to move over and about:
Golden kernels of Maize Tree and coral red beans of Tzʼite Tree.
With which she will form and shape her divination.
From ruby red; coral red divining beans of Coral Tree.

body:
"Invoke us so that we might be invoked!"
"Remember us so that we might be remembered!"
"Enter, then, Ancient Word; enter, then, Ancestral Tradition.
You who are those known as:
Iyom, Mamom: Midwife, Matchmaker
Qatiʼt, Qamam: Our Grandmother, Our Grandfather
Xpiyakok: He who Sprouts forth from Tortoise-Shell Earth; X-peya-kok
Ixmuqane: She of Buried Maize Seed-Ancestral Tooth Ix-muq-kan-eey
"May they come forth into Being at Sowing, at Dawning: Chawaxoq, Saqiroq.
Upon our invocation, upon our incantation, upon our remembrance.
Of Formed People, of Shaped People, of Carved People, of Sculpted People."
"So be it! May it come to pass!"
"May your names be shown, may your names be known:
Jun Ajpu Wuch: Ancient One Grandfather Possum, Ancestor of Dawn
Jun Ajpu Utiw: Ancient One Grandfather Coyote, Ancestor of Dusk
Jun Ajpu Wuch: Nagual of Quetzalcoatl; Ancestral Lord One Hunter Possum
Jun Ajpu Utiw: Nagual of Tezcatlipoca; Ancestral Lord One Hunter Coyote
Kamul Alom: Twice Bearer of Descendants; Great Grandmother
Kamul Kʼajolom: Twice Begetter of Descendants; Great Grandfather
Saqi-Nim Aq: Great White Jabali-Peccary, Old White-Haired Ancestress
Saqi-Nima Sis: Great White Coati-Kinkajou; Old White-Haired Ancestress
AjKʼuwal: Worker of Precious Green Jade
AjYamanik: Worker of Translucent Emeralds
AjChʼut: Artisan Sculptors; Wood Carver
AjTzʼalam: Artisan Woodworkers; Sawyer
AjRaxa Laq: Maker of Blue-Green Plate; Sacrificer of Jade Plate
AjRaxa Tzel: Maker of Blue-Green Bowl; Sacrificer of Turquoise Bowl
AjQʼol: Incense Maker; Resin Gatherer; Gatherer of Pine Resin
AjToltekat: Toltec Artisan, Toltec Artist; Refined Artists of Toltec Tradition
Ratiʼt Qʼij: Grandmother of Day; Diviner of Days
RaTʼit Saq: Grandmother of Dawn; Diviner of Dawn
As you will be invoked by those who will be Our Providers; Our Sustainers.
Our Formed Ones, Our Shaped Ones: QaTzʼaq, QaBʼit."

From soft knotless amber wood of Tzʼiteʼ Tree; Coral Tree.

"Let it be done; let it be known.
Let revelation be revealed through work of divination.
Let golden seeds of maize be thrown.
Let coral red beans of Tzʼite be scattered.
To reveal just how these formed being that are shaped being.
That are carved being that are crafted being.
Will be brought forth into being!"
"Let it be done, let it be finished.
Pass your hands over scattered Maize kernels.
Pass your hands over scattered Tzʼite.
…Coral red Tzʼite beans; golden yellow Maize seeds…

May golden kernels be thrown.
May coral red beans be scattered.
To reveal essence of their nature, nature of their matter.
Flesh of body; body of being.
What will be essence of substance of flesh of these molded beings?
These modeled beings of molded and modeled matter.
From what then shall they be made?"
Let it be done:
"Let us let them perform their forming and shaping.
In order to divine work of Formers, Shapers.
In their work forming Formed Beings.
In their work shaping Shaped Beings."
"Let us let them try their luck.
Let us let them consult their Way of Seeing; their Way of Knowing; their Way of
Divining.
Through casting and scattering of seeds.
Casting and scattering of beans.
Forming and shaping of seeds.
Forming and shaping of beans.
Counting of seeds.
Counting of beans.
Through which to perform our divination and all that it reveals."
"Let them make another attempt at bring forth knowledge.
To bring forth knowing that comes forth from seeing and knowing of divination.
In our effort to reveal what will be revealed.
Through our revelation of our divination with it seeing and knowing.
Of that which must be done."
"Let it be known; let it be revealed; let it be divined.
So that we may know what will be essence of their flesh.
Essence of flesh of their bodies.
Bodies of those who will be Formed.
